title: Miri and piri as thought
hook: spiritual and worldly life held together, not split

segments.voice: Yesterday, Granth and Panth: the Guru carried by a book and by a people. Your line: book and people.

Two swords, worn at once. That's how Sikh tradition remembers Guru Hargobind on the day he took up the guruship: one sword at each side. You met him and his two swords in year one. When people asked why, the answer came in a pair of words: one sword for miri, one for piri. It's easy to live as if life comes in two drawers: one for the job, the rent, the news, who does the dishes; another, smaller, for prayer or quiet. Today is about refusing the two drawers. Not the swords themselves, but the thought behind them.
screen: `TWO SWORDS, WORN AT ONCE.` → `MIRI. PIRI.` → `NOT TWO DRAWERS.`

segments.voice: Miri is worldly authority: the life of rule, justice, work, the public square. Piri is spiritual authority: the life of prayer, the Word, the inner path. Alongside the two swords, tradition says Guru Hargobind raised the Akal Takht, a seat of worldly authority, facing the Harmandir, the house of prayer. Two buildings, looking at each other. Not one behind the other, not one in another city. Facing. The idea didn't start with the swords. Guru Arjan, in the var in Raag Gujri, says it with ordinary words. In paraphrase: meeting the true Guru, a person finds the complete way, and is set free while laughing, playing, dressing and eating. Notice the verbs. Laughing. Playing. Getting dressed. Eating. Liberation isn't kept in a separate room for special occasions. It happens in the middle of the ordinary. So what does the thought ask? If miri and piri belong together, prayer has to show up at work, and work has to be done as if the Guru were watching. Sikh teachers read the two swords as a call to care about justice as a spiritual duty, and to keep the inner life awake while doing it. A prayer that never touches how you treat people stays in the drawer. A public life with no inner life loses its way. The thought refuses both. Both together.
screen: `MIRI: THE WORLD. PIRI: THE SPIRIT.` · `TWO BUILDINGS, FACING.` · `FREE WHILE LAUGHING AND EATING.` · `PRAYER AT WORK; WORK AS PRAYER.` · then, large: `BOTH TOGETHER.`

segments.voice: Picture the next ordinary task you'll do, dishes, an email, a drive, a diaper, a spreadsheet, and see yourself doing it. Without changing the task at all, carry this same breath and quiet into it, with Waheguru in the back of your mind if you pray. Same task, no drawer at all.
Miri and piri as thought. Worldly life and spiritual life held together, not split: two swords, two buildings facing, one life. Today's word.
screen: `MIRI AND PIRI AS THOUGHT — today's word`.

segments.voice: Your line: both together. Two swords, one life. I'll be here tomorrow.
